proof_question: Was there a real relationship of authority or control?
evidence: Rank, appointment, functional role, communications, unit structure, de facto authority
analysis_note: Formal title helps but is not enough; effective control is the key.

proof_question: Could the accused prevent, punish, discipline, or report crimes?
evidence: Capacity to issue orders, remove personnel, discipline, deploy forces, control resources
analysis_note: The doctrine turns on material ability, not honorific status.

proof_question: Did the superior know or have reason to know crimes were being or had been committed?
evidence: Reports, prior incidents, complaints, media, inspections, scale of violence, patterns
analysis_note: Knowledge may be inferred from circumstances, but inference must be grounded.

proof_question: Did the superior take necessary and reasonable measures before or during crimes?
evidence: Orders, warnings, deployments, restrictions, removal from posts, protective measures
analysis_note: Measures are judged in context of actual capacity and available information.

proof_question: Did the superior respond after crimes became known?
evidence: Investigations, referrals, discipline, cover-up, retention, destruction of records
analysis_note: Post-crime inaction can be evidence of responsibility.
